title: HygieneRoll Replenishment Ontology
scope: A controlled HygieneRoll vocabulary for recurring household hygiene consumption and replenishment planning. It is a project vocabulary, not an industry standard or an official taxonomy.

layers.definition: A concept or distinction HygieneRoll defines. It needs origin_refs and carries no source_ids.
A statement about the external world. A value may be published only with source_ids that resolve to ADMITTED sources in reference/source-register.json.

A number computed deterministically by the replenishment engine from scenario inputs. It needs a formula and an engine operation. It is arithmetic, not an interpretation of evidence, so it needs no source.
A value the user supplies as an assumption about their own household. It is not a measurement, an average, or a benchmark.

statuses.definition: Defined and operationalized in this version.
Identifier and definition held so the boundary is explicit. No value is published and the engine does not read it.

dimensions.definition: Units of one item, as the user labels them. Not comparable across items.
Whole or fractional days, counted from the moment the scenario is entered.
A value from a controlled list.

predicates.definition: The subject is computed from the object.
The subject is an input to the computation of the object.
The subject is a controlled list used to label the object.
The subject is a container that holds the object.
The subject is evaluated against the object.
The subject is never an input to the object.

versioning.scheme: MAJOR.MINOR. Version 0.x signals a working vocabulary.
rules: An identifier is never reused or reassigned to a different meaning.
A change in meaning, unit, or formula retires the identifier and issues a new one. The retired concept keeps its record with status RETIRED and a replaced_by reference.
Adding concepts, predicates, or relationships increments MINOR.
Editorial wording that leaves meaning, unit, and formula unchanged does not change the version.
Removing a layer or changing the meaning of a layer, status, or predicate increments MAJOR.
Each concept records the ontology version in which it was introduced in since.

concepts.definition: A HygieneRoll grouping of recurring household hygiene items: paper hygiene, personal hygiene, household hygiene, or other. A category labels an item. It does not carry a usage rate.
The label a user gives to one counted unit of an item, such as a roll, a pack, or a bottle. It is display only. Units are not converted and are not compared across items or products.
The set of items, and the per-item assumptions, that one user enters for one household scenario. It has no household-size input and no archetype. Each item keeps an independent clock.
Units of an item on hand when the scenario is entered. It must be greater than zero.
Units used per week, normalized from the user's weekly usage or from how long the current supply usually lasts. It restates the user's assumption. It is not a measured rate.
concepts.formula: weekly method: r = weekly_usage; duration method: r = current_quantity / duration_weeks

concepts.definition: What the user enters about use: a usage method, and either weekly usage in item units or typical duration in weeks.
A user-selected percentage, from 0 to 50, that widens usage into a slow and a fast bound. It is a planning allowance. It is not a probability, a confidence interval, or a measured spread.
The slow and fast consumption rates produced by applying the variability allowance to the consumption rate.
concepts.formula: slow = r × (1 − v); fast = r × (1 + v); v = variability_percent / 100

concepts.definition: The whole-day window in which current supply runs out under the fast and slow usage bounds.
concepts.formula: earliest = floor((q / fast) × 7); latest = ceil((q / slow) × 7); at v = 0 both equal round_half_up((q / r) × 7)

concepts.definition: The user's assumption of how many days a replenishment takes to arrive after it is ordered. Zero or more. There is no hidden default.
The extra days of supply the user wants to still have when a replenishment arrives. Zero or more. It is a preference, not an optimal stock level.
The units consumed during the fulfillment lead time at the fast usage bound, rounded up to 0.01.
The safety buffer expressed in item units at the fast usage bound, rounded up to 0.01.
The stock level at which ordering keeps the safety buffer intact under the fast usage bound. It is the stock-level expression of the planning trigger.
The reorder window in days: the depletion interval minus lead time and safety buffer, clamped at zero.
concepts.formula: max(0, depletion − lead_time_days − safety_buffer_days), each end separately

concepts.definition: Units the user usually adds at each replenishment. When left blank, the current supply is used.
The illustrative interval between replenishments: how long one replenishment quantity lasts under the usage bounds. It is not a recommended subscription frequency.
concepts.formula: same day-window rule as the depletion interval, with replenishment_quantity in place of q

concepts.definition: An optional fixed interval, in days, that the user wants to compare against the item's replenishment cadence, such as a subscription schedule they hold or are considering.

Whether a fixed delivery interval falls inside the replenishment cadence window, and by how many days per cycle it drifts from it. A positive drift means supply shrinks each cycle. A negative drift means stock accumulates.
concepts.formula: EARLIER_THAN_WINDOW if interval < cadence.earliest; LATER_THAN_WINDOW if interval > cadence.latest; otherwise WITHIN_WINDOW; drift = interval − cadence, from latest (min) to earliest (max)

concepts.definition: For a given order day and lead time, the days an item would be without supply before the replenishment arrives, at the slow (min) and fast (max) usage bounds. It is scenario arithmetic, not a probability of stockout.
concepts.formula: arrival = order_day + lead_time; max = max(0, ceil(arrival − depletion.earliest)); min = max(0, ceil(arrival − depletion.latest))

concepts.definition: A sensitivity check: the planning trigger re-planned for a longer lead time, and the stockout exposure if the order was placed at the original trigger but arrived late. Offsets are fixed presentation values, not forecasts of delay.
concepts.formula: for each offset s: trigger(depletion, lead_time + s, buffer); stockout_exposure(order_day = trigger.earliest, lead_time + s)

concepts.definition: The item or tied items whose planning trigger begins soonest. Items are not averaged.
concepts.formula: items with minimum planning_trigger.earliest, in input order

concepts.definition: The machine-readable output of one scenario. It holds every input and every derived value under the field names listed in this ontology, with the engine and ontology versions. It has no timestamp, so identical inputs produce an identical record.

A consumption rate measured for a stated population, geography, product, and period by an admitted external source. No value is admitted in this version. The engine never substitutes one for a user assumption.
